hypotheses.name: The Iran file is coalition-captured (NEW — the capture read, tracked as opinion)
hypotheses.d: The claim: on the Iran file, organized coalition pressure — donor networks, primary structure, allied commitments, defense-institutional momentum — outweighs the base's war fatigue, which is why a 'no more wars' White House struck anyway and now substitutes sanctions for settlement rather than sign a visible retreat before the midterms. Mechanisms named, plural: status clock vs electoral clock, sunk cost after declaring victory, lobbies as veto players that raise the price of defection (one interest group among several — any single-key version of this hypothesis is scored separately and currently rejected). Opens at 70%: the strike itself, the 6-month grind, and 'not in a hurry' all fit; capped because the same facts also fit ordinary planning failure plus vanity. Falsifier: a signed de-escalation or negotiated Hormuz reopening BEFORE the midterms — the base's clock winning on the party's most captured file would kill the strong form outright.

hypotheses.name: Nobody’s hurrying on Hormuz — HELD at 60%

Kinetic down, jurisdiction up is the ratchet signature. Capped at +5; the stated tell is what the coast guard does through the Sept 24 visit.

hypotheses.name: NEW · Venezuela was a Hormuz hedge in a drug-war uniform
hypotheses.d: The clearest revealed-preference play on the board — and the reason it opens at 55 rather than higher. Sturdy mechanism first: US Gulf-Coast refineries are plumbed for heavy sour crude, Venezuela sits on the planet's largest heavy reserves, and moving that barrel north through the Caribbean to Texas and Louisiana structurally hedges the one risk that ran live all year — a Hormuz closure. The Aug 28-29 deal (a new operator taking control of ~65bn barrels, about a fifth of Venezuela's reserves) is exactly what this hypothesis predicts, and the reporting frames it in plain words as an alternative to Gulf oil routed through Hormuz. So oil-as-motive is near-certain. What is NOT settled — and what caps this — is premeditation: was Operation Southern Spear a counter-narcotics and regime-change campaign that harvested the oil after the fact, or an oil-security operation in a drug-war uniform from the start? The tell against design is the clock — the deal trailed Maduro's Jan 3 capture by eight months, which reads more like spoils than master plan. Mundane alternative, named and live: drugs, migration politics, regime-change, with the barrel a bonus. Falsifiers — cut hard if export volumes stay token (the $2-2.8bn tranches are a rounding error against control of 65bn bbl), if Gulf-Coast heavy sourcing does not actually swing off the Middle East, or if the fixed infrastructure (GEO-022) never appears. One correction the excitement needs: a canal cannot bypass Hormuz, geography does not work that way — the hedge is source substitution plus Caribbean routing, not a waterway. Real Orinoco or Maracaibo channel-dredging and dedicated heavy-crude terminals WOULD be the premeditation tell. Unconfirmed today; it is the thing to watch.

hypotheses.d: Economic Outcast hit ~60 teapots, tankers and traders and touched no Chinese state major and no bank — Treasury sent the majors a warning letter instead. hypotheses.name: NEW · A pre-announcement leak into oil futures

Split: deliberate leak 45 / mediator-side 20 / skilled opportunism 25 / coincidence 10. This is the only entry in the book whose evidence is timestamped BEFORE the event rather than pattern-matched after — which is why it opens this high. Against it: no episode has surfaced around this week's diplomacy.

hypotheses.d: Cut again. The channels that actually moved this week were Oman, Pakistan and the new Mecca defence pact — Russia was absent from every one of them, and still has not offered the mediation this hypothesis expects. Motive 9/10, documentary evidence 0/10, pre-event evidence never. Cut to 15% if nothing surfaces by Sept 30.

brief.head: Germany blames Russia for explosive drone at Leipzig airport
brief.h: Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt said Russia is responsible for the 4 August drone attack at Leipzig/Halle - explosives found on a drone beside a Ukrainian cargo aircraft at NATO's main airlift hub - and Berlin answered by closing Russia's Bonn consulate by 18 September and the Russian House in Berlin, hours after police defused incendiary devices at a Brandenburg power substation.
brief.t: Read the target, not the drone. Leipzig/Halle is where the alliance rents its heavy lift - Antonov Airlines flies NATO's Strategic Airlift International Solution out of that field - so the cheapest way to slow reinforcement of the eastern flank is not to shoot down a transport but to make its insurer nervous. A device whose detonator failed still did the work: it repriced a civilian charter arrangement the alliance depends on and cannot quickly replace. Berlin's answer is the tell. A consulate, a cultural institute and tighter visas are diplomatic property, not treaty rungs, because there is no rung on the Article 5 ladder for a bomb that did not go off.
brief.context: Name the mechanism: sub-threshold coercion, the deliberate practice of staying one notch below the level at which a defensive alliance is obliged to act, so the target has to choose the response instead of the treaty choosing for them. The rail runs from the 2024 incendiary parcels in air cargo through the Baltic cable drags to this, and the base rate across that record is unforgiving - Europe has attributed dozens of sabotage incidents to Russia and answered nearly all of them with expulsions, listings and building closures, which is a price Moscow has already demonstrated it will pay. The deciding desk is the interior ministry and the domestic security service, not the Bundeswehr, and their binding constraint is evidentiary: an attribution made four weeks after the fact with no suspect in custody is an intelligence judgement, not a prosecutable case. What would change the read is a rung nobody has used - the head of Germany's foreign intelligence service has said sabotage may eventually force NATO to consider Article 5, and a first Article 4 consultation over a hybrid incident would mark the ladder being extended rather than merely climbed.

angles.effect: Gains a name for a pattern and political cover for infrastructure hardening, and takes on the harder problem of having publicly identified an attacker it has no proportionate way to punish
Gains a calibrated demonstration against alliance logistics for the price of two buildings and some visas - and keeps deniability precisely because the device failed to detonate
Pays. SALIS runs on civilian charter aircraft and commercial insurance, and both are repriced by a single defused drone

angles.party: German grid operators and their ratepayers
angles.effect: Pay for the hardening. The Turnow-Preilack node ties the Jaenschwalde plant into the 50Hertz grid, and guarding every such node is a permanent operating cost, not a one-off

dec.kill: A NATO Article 4 consultation, a named suspect in custody, or expulsions reaching the military-attache level would show Berlin means to raise the price above what Moscow has already budgeted. Consulate and institute closures with nothing further inside thirty days confirms the attack was priced correctly.

consp.claim: That the Leipzig drone was not Russian at all - that the attribution was prepared politically before it was established evidentially, and that the device was staged or knowingly allowed to be found in order to manufacture consent for German rearmament and a harder Russia line, with Nord Stream offered as the precedent for who actually benefits from an early official attribution.
consp.spread: Circulating in the Anglophone anti-interventionist blog ecosystem - The Last Refuge ran it as 'Merz Prepares to Blame Russia for Sketchy Leipzig Airport Drone Attack' two days before Berlin made the announcement, and TheDefenseWatch pushed a false-flag framing alongside the Lithuania incidents - and echoed on /pol/'s German-collapse threads
consp.read: This maps onto the Nord Stream frame, where an initial official attribution was later complicated by reporting that pointed elsewhere, and that precedent is the whole source of its purchase. The checkable kernel is a real evidentiary gap: the attribution landed four weeks after the incident, no suspect is in custody, no public evidence has been released, and a short-range quadcopter implies an operator who was physically nearby and has not been found. What the frame smuggles in is the jump from 'the public evidence is thin' to 'therefore it was staged' - intelligence attributions routinely rest on sourcing that never becomes public, which is exactly what makes them impossible to check and cheap to doubt.

brief.head: Bessent says the US will sanction an Iranian bank every week
brief.h: At the G20 finance meeting in Asheville on Tuesday the Treasury Secretary said Washington would announce a bank sanction this week and another the week after - 'we are going to economically asphyxiate this regime' - while Qatar said mediation to reopen Hormuz was under way and Iran's parliament speaker threatened to stop all Gulf oil exports.
brief.t: The innovation is the cadence, not the target. A sanction is an event and events get absorbed; a published weekly schedule converts the same instrument into a metronome that runs against the other side's decision clock, which is why Bessent announced the rhythm before naming a single bank. Follow the mechanism to its end and the terminal rung is cutting an institution out of dollar clearing altogether - the step Treasury keeps describing and has not taken, because it is the one that also taxes allied and Asian banks. Iran's reply is the mirror instrument: Qalibaf's line that if Iran cannot export from the Gulf then nobody will is a chokepoint toll dressed as a threat, and it is the only lever priced in the same currency.
brief.context: Date the rail. This is the post-1971 dollar-clearing system used as ordnance, and the near precedent is maximum pressure in 2018-2020, which achieved roughly what is being achieved now - the rial past two million to the dollar, inflation at 66 percent in July - and did not move the file's owner. Hold that base rate: sanctions campaigns aimed at denying revenue usually succeed at denying revenue, and campaigns aimed at changing a regime's behaviour succeed in something like one case in twenty. The deciding desk is OFAC rather than State, and its binding constraint is allied tolerance, which is why the escalation is sold as a weekly drip rather than delivered at once. The tell that this is real rather than rhythmic is a blocking designation on a top-ten Chinese or Indian institution - the first one that would cost Washington something - and until it appears the pressure lands on Iranian households, not on the Guards, whose permit regime at Hormuz becomes more valuable as licensed cargo becomes scarcer.

angles.effect: Gains a visible weekly deliverable and an allied show of support, bought with an announced schedule rather than the terminal designation that would test it
Gains, perversely. Scarcity raises the rent on every permit its Persian Gulf Strait Authority issues, so the tighter the squeeze the more valuable the institution that sells exceptions to it
Pay first and pay most. A two-million rial and 66 percent inflation are the transmission mechanism, and they arrive years ahead of any political effect
Pay the compliance bill now, and far more if a large Chinese counterpart is designated - which is precisely why that designation keeps not happening

dec.kill: A blocking designation on a top-ten Chinese or Indian bank inside thirty days would mean Washington will bear cost and the asphyxiation language is operational. A run of weekly announcements confined to small or already-isolated institutions through October means the cadence is the product.

consp.claim: That the US Energy Information Administration's failure to publish its weekly oil supply data, blamed on technical difficulties, is deliberate - that the numbers are being withheld because they would show a real crude and product shortfall the administration cannot afford to have visible before the November midterms.
consp.spread: A running /pol/ thread headed 'US suddenly can't publish oil supply data due to technical difficulties', and repeated across energy-trading accounts on X
consp.read: This is the strongest species of board narrative, because the kernel is entirely checkable and only the inference is contested: a federal statistical agency genuinely did stop publishing on schedule, and the gap is a fact anyone can verify. The frame then supplies motive, and the base rate runs against it - statistical outages are usually what they say they are, and EIA has had systems and contractor failures before with no political content. What makes it stick is that the administration has an obvious interest in the number, which is the condition under which even an innocent outage becomes unfalsifiable in public.

brief.head: Trump says the US position on the Falklands is under review
brief.h: Asked in the Oval Office about reports the Pentagon had drafted a plan to oppose British sovereignty over the islands unless London moves toward a 5 percent defence spending target, Trump said 'I always review every position - that's just one of many', unsettling a formal US neutrality that has stood since 1982.
brief.t: This is not a South Atlantic story, it is an alliance-pricing story. What is being tested is whether recognition can be spent like money in a budget argument - and recognition has a property that makes it unusually attractive to whoever holds it, because withdrawing it costs the withdrawing state nothing fiscally and costs the target almost everything symbolically. The reported Pentagon framing, reassessing US backing for European possessions as leverage on allies who declined to support the Iran campaign, tells you the deciding desk is whoever keeps the ledger on Epic Fury, not the Western Hemisphere bureau. Note who is embarrassed by the gift: Buenos Aires has been careful rather than triumphal, because a sovereignty claim advanced as a favour from Washington is a claim Washington can recall.
brief.context: The rail is a 44-year-old ambiguity that has been load-bearing precisely because nobody touched it. Since 1982 the United States has recognised de facto British administration while formally taking no position on sovereignty - and materially assisted Britain anyway, with Ascension, intelligence and Sidewinders, once Reagan's initial neutrality collapsed. The gap between declared neutrality and actual support is the asset now being waved around. Base rate: threats to withdraw recognition as alliance leverage are common and almost never executed, because recognition is cheap to threaten and expensive to spend - once withdrawn it cannot be quietly restored, and every other American security guarantee is repriced by the precedent. Milei is the variable that makes this different from the last time it was floated: a Washington-aligned president in Buenos Aires makes the threat credible in a way it has never been, and also makes it worthless to him if it stays a threat.

angles.effect: Gains a costless lever on European defence budgets - the threat does its work whether or not it is executed, which is the definition of an efficient one
Gains a nationalist windfall it did not have to earn, at the price of owing its best card to a foreign patron who can take it back
Pays. The garrison and the self-determination case have rested on unspoken American backing, and unspoken has just become under review in the middle of a defence-spending negotiation
Carry the actual risk and hold no seat - roughly 3,600 people whose status is being used as a chip in an argument about somebody else's budget

dec.kill: A State Department restatement of the traditional neutrality line, or the review lapsing unmentioned within sixty days, means this was leverage theatre and should be scored as such. A changed US vote or statement at the UN decolonisation committee, or an explicit public linkage to a UK spending figure, means recognition has actually been monetised - and every American ally will price that precedent.

brief.head: China warns Taiwan of consequences over Pacific summit seat
brief.h: Beijing's Pacific envoy Qian Bo called Taipei's presence at the 55th Pacific Islands Forum in Koror 'very inappropriate' and warned of consequences, after host Palau seated Taiwan's foreign minister Lin Chia-lung alongside the Chinese delegation at the opening ceremony and Beijing issued travel warnings for Palau.
brief.t: The dispute is over a chair, and the chair is the whole asset. Beijing is not defending territory here, it is defending a norm - that Taiwanese officials cannot appear as officials in any multilateral room - because that norm is what keeps the eventual reunification claim administrative rather than contested. Palau's only leverage is protocol and it used it: President Surangel Whipps Jr. put the two delegations in the same row deliberately, which is the sharpest instrument available to a state of 18,000 people. Follow the money on the other side and the counter-instrument is already visible in the travel warning, because Palau's economy is tourism and Chinese group travel is a tap Beijing has closed before.
brief.context: Name the mechanism: salami tactics in Schelling's sense - slices too thin for any one of them to be worth fighting over, which is why the recognition ledger moves without anyone calling it a crisis. The rail is a retail market. Eleven states and the Vatican still recognise Taipei, three of them - Palau, the Marshall Islands and Tuvalu - are Forum members, and every defection since 2019, Solomon Islands then Kiribati then Nauru, was bought individually with loans, fisheries access and infrastructure. Taiwan's count has gone from fifteen to eleven in seven years, and it holds its seat here as a Forum development partner, a status it topped up with a $2m donation to the Secretariat in July. The deciding desks are customs, fisheries licensing and tourism approvals, not the PLA. The duller scoreboard is the informative one: whether the leaders' communique names China's 6 July submarine-launched missile test that fell near Tuvalu's exclusive economic zone, and whether Kiribati's whataboutist defence of it - why does nobody ask about American tests - carries the room.

angles.effect: Gains a demonstration aimed at the other ten recognisers by making one small host visibly pay, which is far cheaper than buying another switch
Gains standing, Taiwanese money and a domestic story about not being pushed around, and absorbs tourism coercion it has absorbed before
Gains the scarce good - an official appearance in a multilateral room - at the price of making its remaining friends into targets

angles.party: The small Forum states with no stake in the fight
angles.effect: Pay. Their climate, fisheries and narcotics agenda gets crowded out by exactly the great-power sideshow their leaders publicly asked to avoid

dec.kill: A leaders' communique that names the July missile test, with no Chinese economic action against Palau within ninety days, would mean 'consequences' was rhetoric. A suspension of Chinese tour groups, a fisheries or customs action, or a recognition switch by a Forum member inside six months means it was an instrument - and the ledger moves again.

brief.head: Nepal begins mass burials as flood toll passes 1,000
brief.h: Six days after part of a glacier sheared into the Lhende Khola above the Bhote Koshi and sent a surge up to nine metres high down the valley in half an hour, Nepal has recovered more than 1,000 bodies with close to 3,900 people still missing, and has started burying the unidentified after DNA sampling.
brief.t: The number that will still matter in a year is not the toll, it is 748 megawatts. Nepal's development strategy since 2015 has been run-of-river hydropower built into glacial valleys and sold to India - the country's principal export is electrons - and roughly a tenth of national generating capacity sat in the valley this came down. So this is not first of all a weather story, it is an asset-siting story: the plants were placed directly beneath slopes being destabilised by thawing permafrost, on the assumption that the last century's hazard map still describes the next one. The other half is jurisdictional. The trigger was on the Tibetan side of the border and bodies were carried some 240 kilometres into India, in a basin with no shared early-warning system at all.
brief.context: The rail is the Hindu Kush Himalaya hazard belt and a pattern it has now produced three times in five years - Chamoli in 2021, South Lhonak in Sikkim in 2023, and this - each one destroying hydropower built after the last one, because the economics of a run-of-river scheme demand precisely the steep high-valley sites where the hazard concentrates. Glaciologists are explicit that this is the direction of travel rather than an outlier: Jakob Steiner of the University of Graz described a lower glacier section coming away as though cut with a knife and called it the new normal. The deciding desks here are not diplomatic - they are whoever writes Nepal's project siting rules and whoever underwrites the hydro debt, because a lender that keeps financing the same siting assumption is the mechanism by which the pattern repeats. What would change the read is a moratorium on new high-valley schemes, or an upstream hydrological data-sharing arrangement with China, which does not exist because the water starts in Tibet and Beijing has never shared that data on terms Kathmandu could rely on.

consp.claim: That the glacier collapse was engineered - that HAARP, the ionospheric research facility in Alaska, caused the landslide and flood across Nepal and Tibet, making this a man-made disaster rather than a natural one.
consp.spread: Loud on X within hours of the collapse, including a 26 August post by a New York hedge-fund manager stating flatly that HAARP caused it, then recycled across the weather-modification account network; AFP and academic geomorphologists have since published debunks
consp.read: This is the weather-control frame, which recurs after every large sudden natural disaster and does a specific psychological job: it supplies an agent. The checkable part runs hard against it - the trigger has been reconstructed in a published study as a domino rock-and-ice avalanche, roughly 5.5 million cubic metres of progressive rock collapse releasing about 8.3 million cubic metres of mixed material, and a geomorphologist at Grenoble stated there is no mechanism by which an ionospheric facility could affect it. What the narrative is downstream of is a genuinely unsatisfying explanation: 'the permafrost holding the mountain together thawed' is a diffuse cause with nobody to blame, and diffuse causes are exactly the vacuum a directed-energy story fills.

lesson: In June 1914, weeks before the war, Winston Churchill stood up in the Commons as First Lord of the Admiralty and asked Parliament to buy 51 percent of the Anglo-Persian Oil Company. The argument was not commercial. He had converted the Royal Navy from Welsh coal to oil for speed, and in doing so had made the fleet dependent on a liquid Britain did not produce - so the state bought the producer rather than trust the market to sell to it in a crisis. That is the rail under today's Venezuela announcement, and it is worth naming precisely: a defence ministry taking an equity position in a foreign oil venture is not an investment, it is a supply guarantee bought with a balance sheet instead of a contract, and it appears whenever a military finds its fuel on the far side of somebody else's chokepoint. The Pentagon's Office of Strategic Capital holding 35 percent of a Venezuelan venture, with a right to buy a fifth of the output at cost for the reserve and the military, is Churchill's instrument with the serial numbers filed off. What the precedent predicts is the part nobody announces on day one. State equity creates a state obligation to defend the asset, and it converts every subsequent local political change into a foreign-policy problem: APOC's stake bought Britain fuel for two wars and then bought it Mossadegh's nationalisation in 1951 and a coup in 1953, because a century-long claim on another country's principal resource outlives the government that granted it. So here is the falsifiable version rather than the cautionary tale. If this is a supply guarantee in the Churchill mould, the fixed infrastructure follows the equity - awarded dredging, a dedicated heavy-crude terminal, upgraders - because barrels you own but cannot move are not a guarantee; if eighteen months pass with the stake in place and no funded logistics award, then this was a fee extracted from a client government rather than a rail, and the analogy should be marked down accordingly.

lecture.title: The Economic Weapon: Why Sieges Make the Wars They Mean to Prevent

sections.t: Treasury designated roughly sixty Chinese “teapot” refiners — the small plants buying discounted Iranian crude — while touching no Chinese state major and no bank. The same week, central banks bought a record 288.9 tonnes of gold in the quarter gold fell over 20%. Two stories, one machine.

sections.h: Follow the money, name the mechanism
sections.t: A reserve manager buying into a 20% drawdown is not trading. He is hedging ACCESS — the risk that an asset held abroad gets switched off by its host government — and gold is the only large reserve asset with no counterparty who can flip that switch. Name the mechanism: the ECONOMIC WEAPON, using the financial plumbing whose hubs one country owns to inflict a siege without laying one. Iran discounts crude to Chinese teapots paying through dollar-touching chains; Treasury designates them; the IRGC's Strait Authority recoups the shortfall in Hormuz tolls. Sanction and gold bar are one transaction seen from two ends.

sections.h: Deep history I — the blockade that became an idea
sections.t: The economic weapon has a birthday and a founding failure. The birthday is November 1806, when Napoleon's Berlin Decrees declared the British Isles blockaded — the Continental System, an attempt to beat a maritime power by closing a continent's markets to it. It succeeded at nothing except generating enforcement. Portugal would not comply, so France invaded in 1807 and got the Peninsular War, the ulcer that bled the Grande Armée for six years. Alexander I quit the system in December 1810 because it was ruining Russian trade, and in 1812 Napoleon marched east to enforce it. The blockade never defeated Britain; it manufactured the two wars that destroyed the blockader. Sanctions require enforcement, and enforcement against a determined leakage path tends toward conquest. The second case mattered because it worked. The Allied blockade of Germany ran from 1914 through the armistice and was lifted only when Germany signed at Versailles in June 1919. German official estimates put civilian deaths from malnutrition near 424,000 — contested, and historians still argue how much was blockade and how much German agricultural mismanagement. But perception makes policy, and a generation concluded hunger had beaten an undefeated army. So they institutionalized it as a PEACE instrument: Article 16 of the League Covenant made sanctions automatic against an aggressor, and Wilson in 1919 put it in words no Treasury official would dare use today — “A nation that is boycotted is a nation that is in sight of surrender. Apply this economic, peaceful, silent, deadly remedy and there will be no need for force.” The weapon was invented to ABOLISH war; the rest of the century refutes that sentence.

sections.h: Deep history II — the failures that define our problem
sections.t: ABYSSINIA, 1935. Italy invaded Ethiopia; the League invoked Article 16 — exempting oil, coal and steel, and never closing the Suez Canal, which Britain controlled and through which Italian troopships sailed. Mussolini won anyway. The sanctions were real enough to enrage and too porous to stop, and the lesson is sharper than “sanctions don't work”: a sanction calibrated to spare the sender teaches the target that the sender is deterred too. Then the second-order effect. Nicholas Mulder's argument in The Economic Weapon is that the interwar regime deterred small states and PROVOKED large ones. Italy, Germany and Japan drew the same conclusion from the 1930s — dependence on seaborne trade was a vulnerability an enemy could switch off at will, and the answer was autarky, self-sufficiency taken by force. Lebensraum and the Co-Prosperity Sphere were ideological projects; they were also sanctions-proofing programs. Japan is the proof case. Washington embargoed scrap iron in 1940, then froze Japanese assets on 26 July 1941; America supplied roughly 80% of Japan's oil, and with Britain and the Dutch East Indies following, Japan lost about 88% of its oil imports. Reserves would last three years at peace, half that at war — Nagano's image was of a patient wasting away, every month of compliance leaving Japan weaker against the enemy it expected to fight. Pearl Harbor came in December. And the detail that turns story into discipline: the freeze was never meant to be total. Roosevelt intended a licensing regime keeping oil flowing so the tap stayed usable as leverage; officials in State and Treasury administered it so strictly that no licences issued and the flow stopped. The sanction that helped produce Pearl Harbor was substantially an organizational outcome, not a presidential decision — Allison's Essence of Decision, live. Before inferring “Iran's strategy” from one action, ask which bureau took it.

sections.h: The pattern — and where it breaks
sections.t: The leakage path is always the whole story — not the designation list, the leak: Portugal and Russia in 1806, Beira and Pretoria in 1966, Chinese teapots now. NOW THE BREAK. Japan in 1941 had a military option that promised to SOLVE its resource problem: seize the Dutch East Indies and own the oil. Iran has none — it fought its war, lost the conventional exchange, and has played its asymmetric card, the Hormuz toll. Nor did 1914 face an alternative supplier: Iran's is the world's second-largest economy, which the sanctioner just spared. Less Pearl Harbor, more Rhodesia.

MULDER says the siege provokes: strangulation drives large states to autarky, then preemption. DREZNER says sanctions are cheap theater — Hufbauer's data give a third success rate at best, near zero against great powers. The 2026 evidence buries neither: it splits by SIDE, and the split is the finding. On the TARGET Mulder scores: gold, stockpiles, payment rails, enrichment acceleration under maximum pressure. On the SENDER Drezner scores harder — the carve-outs. Sixty teapots and not one bank is not escalation; it is the sanctioner taking its own threat hostage, because hitting a Chinese bank endangers the dollar system that makes the hammer heavy.

The 2015 architecture is not coming back (high confidence): the 2022 freeze of Russian reserves turned the settlement network into an instrument; a hedge once bought is not resold. Expect bifurcation, not de-dollarization (moderate-high). EICHENGREEN is right that currencies erode glacially; the WEAPON depreciates faster than the CURRENCY. The bolder call (moderate): the most dangerous decade is the one in which the weapon still works but no longer terrifies. Mulder's mechanism fires in the transition — invested in escaping, not finished, expecting strangulation regardless. For China, the 2030s — so Economic D-Day may SHORTEN the fuse it was meant to lengthen. FALSIFIER: designate a major Chinese state bank; if Beijing cuts Iranian purchases within a quarter, I am wrong. Two centuries say the economic weapon does not replace war — it sorts the world into blocs that survive each other's sieges, then gives the survivors a reason to fight.

Nicholas Mulder, The Economic Weapon (2022) — published weeks before the Russia sanctions matched its template. Farrell & Newman, “Weaponized Interdependence” (2019) — it called the 2022 playbook and the chip controls in advance. Eichengreen, Exorbitant Privilege — the counterweight.

Nothing this afternoon adds to it - logged so the fire is dated once and not re-counted.
NOT fired, and it is the limit of the above: the hulls are Saudi and South Korean, not US-flagged. No confirmed American deaths, no struck US hull. The intercepted-volley equilibrium has not broken.

NOT fired, checked and logged so the non-fire is scoreable: no blocking designation on a top-ten Chinese bank; no Kremlin acceptance of any limited ceasefire; no ferry requisition, reserve mobilization or missile dispersal near Taiwan; no summit-cancellation signal; no verified IRGC or Basij defection; no strike on Kharg's loading terminals; no awarded dredging or terminal contract in Venezuela.

WIRE HYGIENE - a gap this board just found in itself.
